BiblicalUsage: Naqar means to bore or dig out, to pierce or quarry, and it is used for eyes and for rocks. In 1 Samuel 11:2 Nahash the Ammonite offers peace on condition that he may thrust out all their right eyes, and lay it for a reproach upon all Israel, and in Isaiah 51:1 the people are told to look to the rock whence they are hewn, and to the hole of the pit whence they are digged.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the same verb that gouges out an eye also digs a people out of a rock, because the digging is either cruelty or creation; nahash would dig out eyes for spite, and the Lord digs a people out of the pit for salvation.
